# What is the Plaid Trial plan?

The Plaid Trial plan provides free access to Plaid's production APIs. You can connect real financial accounts, call production endpoints, and build projects — no business registration, security questionnaire, or sales process required.

## Who can sign up

The Trial plan is available to developers who:

  * Are located in the United States or Canada
  * Do not already have an existing Plaid Production or Limited Production account

US and Canadian institutions are available on Trial plans, all other institutions are not currently available on this plan type. To get started, go to dashboard.plaid.com/signup.

## Agreements

Applying for a Trial plan requires accepting Plaid's standard Master Services Authorization Agreement (MSA). 

In the Agreements step of the application you'll check "I agree to the latest Plaid Master Services Authorization Agreement," along with attestations about keeping your accounts, data, and code secure. The application can't be submitted without these.

# API Reference

#### Comprehensive reference for integrating with Plaid API endpoints

API endpoints and webhooks

For documentation on specific API endpoints and webhooks, use the navigation menu or search.

API access

To gain access to the Plaid API, create an account on the Plaid Dashboard. Once you've completed the signup process and acknowledged our terms, we'll provide a live `client_id` and `secret` via the Dashboard.

API protocols and headers

The Plaid API is JSON over HTTP. Requests are POST requests, and responses are JSON, with errors indicated in response bodies as `error_code` and `error_type` (use these in preference to HTTP status codes for identifying application-level errors). All responses come as standard JSON, with a small subset returning binary data where appropriate. The Plaid API is served over HTTPS TLS v1.2 to ensure data privacy; HTTP and HTTPS with TLS versions other than 1.2 are not supported. Clients must use an up to date root certificate bundle as the only TLS verification path; certificate pinning should never be used.

## Trial plan

For developers in the US and Canada who sign up on or after April 15, 2026, Plaid offers a Trial plan — a free way to use Plaid with real production data before applying for full Production access. Trial plans are auto-approved for most developers and support up to 10 Production Items. Eight core products are included: Auth, Transactions (including Transactions Refresh), Balance, Identity, Assets, Liabilities, Investments (including Investments Refresh), and Statements. Trial plan developers also have access to OAuth institutions without needing to complete the full Production registration process.

To start a Trial plan, create a Dashboard account and verify your email address, then complete the Trial plan application form.

If you need more than 10 Items, or need products not included in the Trial bundle, you will need to apply for full Production access.

## Limited Production

Note: As of April 15, 2026, new Limited Production signups are no longer available for developers in the US and Canada. If you are a new US/CA developer, see "Trial plan" above. Existing Limited Production customers retain access.

Limited Production is a special mode of the Production environment that is available for some Plaid products and can be used to try the Plaid API with real data before obtaining full Production access. In Limited Production, you have access to Plaid's Production server and can make a limited number of free API calls, but your API usage is capped and some functionality is unavailable. Unlike Sandbox, Limited Production is not a separate environment from Production. For more details on Limited Production, see Testing with Real Data in Limited Production.
